title.narrative: ROAF/GW/Improving urban governance and access to basic services for green and inclusive local development in Guinea-Bissau - Nô Misti Disinvolvimentu Local

description.narrative: Guinea-Bissau has witnessed a rapid growth of its urban population in recent years. While in 1997 only 22.5% of the population lived in urban areas, this proportion had almost doubled (44.2%) by 2020. Whilst the capital Bissau remains as the main political and economic hub of the country, regional centres such as Gabú and Bafatá, among others, have also gained importance as they have seen their population has increased. All urban centres in the country suffer from critical governance issues, with lack of consistent and structured institutional involvement to support urban planning and management, underlying by structural political instability. As a result, levels of access to basic services and infrastructure are critically low (e.g., only 25% of the population has access to improved sanitation). In addition, climate change poses an increasing threat to the country, which has 19% of its land surface under 10 metres above sea level. Several efforts, supported by different partners such as the European Union, have seen advances in areas like water and energy supply and waste management. However, a more structured and holistic approach to urban development action in the country is still lacking. This initiative aims at closing this gap: it will improve the living conditions of urban populations in Guinea Bissau, with for objective to strengthen urban sector governance and the framework for dialogue on inclusive and climate-resilient urban development. This corresponds to the 1st Specific Objective (SO1) of the EU Programme on Green and Inclusive Cities in Guinea-Bissau, fully under UN-Habitat’s responsibility (EUR 9,850,000), which basically constitutes the object of this Project document. [(NB: this EU Programme has two more specific objectives i.e., SO2 that focuses on the reduction of marine and terrestrial pollution linked to the consumption and production of solid waste (especially plastic waste) in Bissau (EUR 6 million), and SO3 that aims to improve sustainable access to drinking water and basic sanitation services for secondary cities in Guinea-Bissau (EUR 5 million). Therefore, the whole EU Green and Inclusive Cities Programme in Guinea-Bissau has a total budget of EUR 21 million, with potential additional EUR 10 million from the European Investment Bank (EIB) under SO2 – feasibility study is on-going).] Therefore, the Project entails an ideal combination of policy and normative measures that aim to provide the framework for urban development in Guinea-Bissau, along with capacity-building activities at different government levels and the opportunity to test these policies and capacities in practice via physical interventions in the targeted cities. It includes 3 outputs, namely: OUTPUT 1. Institutional dialogue and monitoring mechanisms on sustainable urban management are strengthenend OUTPUT 2. Capacities of local, regional and national authorities on integrated urban planning are strengthened. OUTPUT 3. Local basic sanitation services are upgraded and public green spaces improved.
